pr_title: sql/schemachanger: add support for upgrading declarative schema changer elements
pr_body:
This patch adds support for migrating declarative schema changer elements by doing the following:

Fixes: #92605, #91594

1. Eliminate the secondary index partial element.
2. Add an upgrade to convert secondary index partial elements for ongoing schema changes.
3. Add testing to validate that this logic works correctly in a mixed version state.
4. Address a bug between partial secondary indexes and dropped columns to ensure references are correctly cleaned up.
5. Add support inside restore for upgrading declarative schema changer elements.
6. Apply upgrades to schema changer elements during job adoption
7. Add mixed version tests for validating upgrades for schema changer elements during backup/restore
8. Add an upgrade for TXN_DROPPED state and update the corpus debug command to apply upgrades
9. Fixed incorrect version numbering in the builder (needed to support mixed version tests properly)
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/96925)

issue_context.title: scpb: element model migrations for 23.1
issue_context.body:
The partial predicate should be a nullable `Expression` field in `scpb.SecondaryIndex`.

It's not enough to change the protobuf definitions, though. To make this change compatible with mixed-version clusters, this needs to be:
1. version-gated
2. accompanied with a cluster upgrade step which migrates the schema changer state slice of all existing descriptors
3. also accompanied by a `RunRestoreChanges` step to migrate the state in descriptors restored from a 22.2 backup (we no longer need to worry about older backups, thankfully)
4. tested, all of it.

The implementation will serve as a template for how to do schema changer element model migrations in the future.

Jira issue: CRDB-21880

Epic: CRDB-19164
comments:

- if we can move the TypeT in the ColumnType to Column now, then we should
- Column virtual-ness should be moved out of ColumnType to Column
cc @Xiang-Gu wrt NOT NULL

TIL, Is this a recent change? I thought we could take a backup and restore at an arbitrary later version. Do we now enforce restoring at version `n` or `n+1` if the backup was taken at version `n`?

review_comments: Will this sneak through without being caught by the upgrade?
Good point we should double version gate this. The first will ensure that this element is no longer generated the second will migrate existing stuff.
Actually, thinking about this more we do have job adoption migration, which will block the sneaking of this. So, if a connection creates a job it will get fixed on adoption. @chengxiong-ruan
This is right since once the maxVersion is active we no longer emit the element.
